profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Dallas - Downtown Dallas) is located at 1950 North Stemmons Freeway Suite 2033, Dallas, TX 75207. The operator publishes a footprint of 80447 square feet and 6.66 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including HITRUST CSF, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, SSAE 18. ERCOT, the Texas grid operator, forecast in July 2026 that statewide peak power demand would roughly double by 2032, from a record of about 91,308 megawatts set that July to roughly 175,000 megawatts, with ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas citing "a massive influx of data centers" alongside population and broader economic growth as the dominant driver, per the Texas Tribune. ERCOT identified evening hours, when solar generation stops and battery reserves deplete, as the critical supply gap requiring additional natural gas capacity; Texas responded in 2023 by creating the $10 billion Texas Energy Fund loan program, which has financed 5,000 megawatts of new natural gas generation across eight projects so far, with another 2,300 megawatts under review. Texas solar capacity more than doubled between 2023 and 2025, and battery storage capacity tripled over the same period.

Texas is now forgoing at least $1.3 billion a year in sales tax revenue through its data center exemption, first enacted in 2013 when facilities were far smaller, with the state comptroller projecting the cost will reach $1.8 billion by fiscal year 2030; annual revenue loss ran only $5 million to $30 million from 2014 through 2022 before the post-2023 AI boom drove the sharp increase, according to Texas Tribune reporting. To qualify, smaller facilities of at least 100,000 square feet must create at least 20 jobs paying 120% of the area median salary and invest $200 million over five years, earning up to 15 years of exemption; larger facilities of at least 250,000 square feet must create 40 qualifying jobs, invest $500 million, and reserve 20 megawatts of transmission capacity, earning up to 20 years of exemption. The exemption covers servers, software, cooling systems, generators, plumbing, and electricity costs. State Senator Joan Huffman has called the growing cost "extremely concerning" and unsustainable, and lawmakers have signaled they may pursue repealing or narrowing the exemption, amid broader public skepticism toward new data center construction in several Texas communities.

reading.body:
Flexential Dallas - Downtown Dallas in Dallas, Texas, publishes 6.66 MW of IT capacity across 80,000 square feet of technical space, operated by Flexential.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 666 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 166 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Flexential Dallas - Downtown Dallas holds 4 published certifications: SOC 1 Type 2 (audited controls over financial reporting processes), SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA), SSAE 18 (the attestation standard underlying SOC reports). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Texas has 23 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 15 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 399.41 MW. Flexential Dallas - Downtown Dallas contributes 6.66 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
